annotations.text:
DROVE — phase-1 concepts for game #4. Five mechanics, one art direction, held constant on purpose: the comparison is the axis that changes the round, not the paint. Each artboard plays live — a 5 s betting gap, the drive building with the value, then a collect or a cut-off — and loops three scripted rounds.

The seed was "you are a sheep in a flock and a wolf takes it all". The mechanic survived intact; the fiction did not. Sheep are the worked example in the CAP under-18 guidance ("‘cuddly’ or ‘cute’ animals", and "characters with similarities to soft toys in particular should be avoided"), the wolf-and-sheep story is in the same high-risk list under "Common fairy tales, like Little Red Ridinghood", and CAP §13/§14 reach the game’s own theme, not only its ads. So the flock became a cattle drive at dusk, drawn at eye level from inside the mob.

No predator is ever drawn. It cannot appear before the crash — that is advance warning of T — and must not be shown at the crash either, which is the horse-fall beat the earlier audits already banned. The hazard is the mob turning and the gate.

Rules held in every scene: value rises from x1.00 and the multiplier is the hero number; one stake, one collect verb, nothing else is tappable and the mob never reacts to a tap; no other animal is ever shown being taken (that is a near-miss); crowd density and dust follow elapsed time only, never the crash time; a win banner only when the round total beats the stake, otherwise RETURNED with the net; session clock, net position and a rules entry on screen in every state.

The animals are rough placeholders — silhouettes, backs and horns, no faces and no mascot. Production art would be pre-rendered sprite sheets sized for low-end Android. Toggle "reducedMotion" on an artboard for the calm version. Stake, balances and net are sample data.

DROVE  (recommended)
Rising only, slow pace. The engine is whack-crash/v3-rising, untouched:
no new maths, no new config id, the committed 10M-round report already covers it.
Reaches every market in the set, Brazil and Portugal included.
The value is attached to how deep you still are in a mob you cannot steer,
which is the most honest crash fantasy on this canvas: there is nothing to do but leave.

SCATTER  (runner-up)
The mob shoulders you back and the value halves. Config whack-crash/v3, also committed.
Dead in Brazil (1.207 Annex I item 14(d)) and Portugal (R1/R22): a falling value fits
none of the permitted round endings there. Everywhere else it is a profile flag away.
Round 3 is the compliance artboard: the value recovers to exactly x1.00 and the collect
returns the stake. RETURNED, net 0.00, and not one win cue fires.

NIGHT FOLD
The cut-off is already decided and you cannot see it. You learn at the break.
Reuses gate-odds-mvp whole: the live chance (RTP ÷ value, floored) stays on screen
and is restated in the past tense after the press, and the wait is a fixed 1.6 s
from the press for every outcome — never tied to anything drawn on screen.
Nigeria and Ghana only, pending the lab letter. My reservation: that is Gate Rush’s
one differentiator and the same two markets, so it ships a second skin of the same bet.

TWO PENS
One stake, one debit, one round id, two pens collected separately.
The only concept here with a new money path, and the only expensive one: the
paper-route/* split ids are retired, so this needs new ids and a committed 10M-round
report each, plus GLI-19 §4.4.2 per-part displays. No partial cash-out in Portugal.
Round 2 is the artboard people forget: pen A comes in at x1.17 and the drive is then
cut off. The round returned 0.58 on a 1.00 stake, so it is shown as a loss. Celebration
is decided on the round total, never on a pen.

STRAYS
Strays fold into the mob and lift the value 5% each. The boosted ids (v2/v4) exist
with committed reports, and the crash hazard already pays for the lift, so the maths
is settled. What is not settled is acceptance: a boosted id needs its own lab sign-off
before any regulated market uses it. Unregulated now, regulated after the letter.
Strictly this is a config family rather than a game, so it can also ride on any of
the other four as a profile flag.

Certification cost, left to right: DROVE — whack-crash/v3-rising  ·  SCATTER — whack-crash/v3  ·  NIGHT FOLD — whack-crash/v3-rising + crashReveal: onCollect  ·  TWO PENS — new config id, stakeParts: 2  ·  STRAYS — whack-crash/v4-rising.
Four of the five are skins on already-certified ids: registerGame(<game>, 'whack-crash') and nothing in core or fairness changes. Two Pens is the exception and the only one that needs fresh simulate reports.
